validation: Desk review of guidance, not empirical agronomic validation

wheat.source_title: NSW Winter crop variety sowing guide 2026, V2 (April 2026) · pp. 4–5, 15, 21

checks.message: Match cultivar and flowering time to regional frost and heat risks; a broad month filter cannot do this.

barley.source_title: NSW Winter crop variety sowing guide 2026, V2 (April 2026) · pp. 40–45

checks.message: Check regional sowing and cultivar traits, including waterlogging tolerance; species-level scores cannot select a variety.

oats.source_title: NSW Winter crop variety sowing guide 2026, V2 (April 2026) · pp. 55–64

checks.message: Choose a grain, hay or grazing variety and its local sowing window; these uses are not interchangeable.

canola.source_title: NSW Winter crop variety sowing guide 2026, V2 (April 2026) · p. 74

checks.message: Check acidity by depth using pHCa tests; the modelled pH-water average cannot assess this.
Check seedbed moisture, nitrogen, hardpans and rotation history.

chickpea.source_title: NSW Winter crop variety sowing guide 2026, V2 (April 2026) · p. 97

checks.message: Check pHCa, aluminium and subsoil chloride; pH-water is not a substitute.
Check late-spring frost and disease risk for the selected variety.

lentil.source_title: NSW Winter crop variety sowing guide 2026, V2 (April 2026) · pp. 140–141

checks.message: Guidance prefers pHCa 6–8; obtain depth-resolved tests rather than converting the modelled pH-water average.
Check salinity, sodicity and subsurface acidity before selecting lentil.

macadamia.source_title: NSW Macadamia grower's guide 2023: new orchards · pp. 9, 18

checks.message: Confirm at least 0.5 m of free-draining rooting depth; the 0–30 cm soil model does not establish depth.
Check local frost exposure and cold-air pooling; monthly mean minima cannot establish a frost-free orchard.

sorghum.source_title: NSW Summer cropping options for northern and central NSW 2022 · pp. 2–5

checks.message: Measure sowing-depth soil temperature and stored soil water; annual air temperature and rainfall cannot establish readiness.
Check cultivar timing against frost and flowering heat; the October–November filter is only a demo window.

cotton.source_title: NSW SOILpak for cotton growers, third edition · A2-3–A2-6 (edition date unverified)

checks.message: Check stored water, infiltration, rooting conditions and a crop water budget.
The soil targets use CaCl2 pH; do not compare them directly with the modelled pH-water average.
Assess waterlogging and drainage design; a water-scenario selection does not establish suitable soil structure.

rice.source_title: NSW Rice growing guide 2021, second edition · pp. 1, 29

checks.message: Verify irrigation volume and a paddock water budget; annual rainfall is not an irrigated water balance.
Check permeability, sodicity and rice land suitability; topsoil clay alone cannot establish these.
Match variety timing and water management to microspore cold risk.

lucerne.source_title: NSW Lucerne for pasture and fodder, third edition (2003) · pp. 8–9, 16

checks.message: Check top-10-cm pHCa with aluminium and test subsoil acidity; the modelled 0–30 cm pH-water value cannot substitute.
Confirm deep rooting conditions, establishment moisture and locally suitable disease-resistant varieties.

grapes.source_title: NSW Climate Vulnerability Assessment: Chardonnay · undated webpage

checks.message: Assess budbreak and bloom frost, seasonal heat and irrigation demand for a selected cultivar; annual means cannot replace stage-specific checks.
This NSW climate reference concerns Chardonnay, not every grape cultivar or use; obtain local variety advice.

olives.source_title: NSW DPI Olive tree crops (26 October 2021)

checks.message: Check drainage, winter chilling and summer humidity for the intended cultivar; the annual climate screen cannot assess these.

citrus.source_title: NSW Australian mandarin production manual (September 2017) · Orchard basics, pp. 7–11

checks.message: General citrus guidance uses CaCl2 pH; a compatible soil profile is needed.
Check drainage, effective depth, rootstock, frost and irrigation water; this mandarin reference does not validate the sweet-orange proxy.

improved_pasture.source_title: NSW DPIRD Perennial ryegrass species guidance · undated webpage

checks.message: Check regional rainfall distribution, summer moisture and heat, fertility and aluminium for perennial ryegrass persistence.
This is a perennial-ryegrass proxy, not a locally selected pasture mixture; confirm species and cultivars.
